Tan]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Nacionalista Party}}|border=darkgray}} [[Nacionalista Party|Nacionalista]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Minority }} '''Samar's 1st congressional district''' is one of the two [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Samar (province)|Samar]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020}} The district consists of the city of [[Calbayog]] and adjacent municipalities of [[Almagro, Samar|Almagro]], [[Gandara, Samar|Gandara]], [[Matuguinao]], [[Pagsanghan]], [[San Jorge, Samar|San Jorge]], [[Santa Margarita, Samar|Santa Margarita]], [[Santo Niño, Samar|Santo Niño]], [[Tagapul-an]] and [[Tarangnan]]. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Stephen James Tan|Stephen James T. Tan]] of the [[Nacionalista Party]] (NP).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 12, 2020}} Prior to its second dissolution in 1965 due to the split of the [[Samar (historical province)|old province of Samar]], the district consisted of the old province's northern municipalities of [[Allen, Northern Samar|Allen]], [[Bobon]], Calbayog, [[Capul]], [[Catarman, Northern Samar|Catarman]], [[Catubig, Northern Samar|Catubig]], [[Gamay, Northern Samar|Gamay]], [[Laoang]], [[Lapinig]], [[Las Navas, Northern Samar|Las Navas]], [[Lavezares]], [[Mondragon, Northern Samar|Mondragon]], [[Palapag]], [[Pambujan]], [[San Antonio, Northern Samar|San Antonio]], [[San Isidro, Northern Samar|San Isidro]], [[San Jose, Northern Samar|San Jose]], and [[San Roque, Northern Samar|San Roque]]. Following the split, Calbayog became part of Western Samar (now known simply as Samar), while the remaining municipalities formed [[Northern Samar]], with each new province gaining distinct representation.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=4221|date=June 19, 1965|title=An Act Creating the Provinces of Northern Samar, Eastern Samar and Western Samar|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l19db |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=October 13, 2024}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Legislature ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
